cards.explanation: The answer is Aaron with Nadab and Abihu plus seventy elders. The LORD names Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, and seventy of Israel's elders (Exodus 24:1). Aaron is Moses' brother (Exodus 4:14). Seventy elders on one invitation? That's a guest list I'd need a mountain of cookie boxes for.

The answer is True, friends. The LORD says, “…and you are to worship at a distance.” (Exodus 24:1). That's what He tells the group to do, and then He says Moses alone shall approach (Exodus 24:2). I think being invited up the mountain and told to keep your distance in the same breath is a lot to take in.

The answer is False. The LORD says, “And the people may not go up with him.” (Exodus 24:2). Moses alone approaches the LORD, and the others must not come near. The people stay down below, and the line for this mountain is very short.

The word is "do," friends. The people all respond with one voice, “All the words that the LORD has spoken, we will do.” (Exodus 24:3). One voice, all of them together. Even my kitchen has never agreed on anything that fast.

The answer is False, bakers. Moses builds the altar at the base of the mountain, along with twelve pillars (Exodus 24:4). And look at the timing: early the next morning, he's up and building. My oven needs a minute to warm up before I do anything.

The pillars stand for the twelve tribes of Israel, friends (Exodus 24:4). One pillar for each tribe, standing at the base of the mountain with the altar. Twelve is double the number of my cookie cutter kids, and I miss all six of them.

The answer is some young men of Israel, bakers. Moses sends them out, and they offer the burnt offerings and sacrifice the young bulls as peace offerings (Exodus 24:5). No names, no titles, just young men of Israel doing the job. I like that, since plenty of good work in my bakery never gets a name stamped on it.

The answer is True, friends. The young men offer burnt offerings and sacrifice young bulls as peace offerings to the LORD (Exodus 24:5). The text puts the bulls and the peace offerings together right there. A big day for the altar, I'd say.
The answer is the altar, friends. Moses puts half of the blood in bowls, and the other half he splatters on the altar (Exodus 24:6). Two halves, two places. The verse keeps careful count.

Moses splatters the blood on the people, bakers. He takes the blood and says, “This is the blood of the covenant that the LORD has made with you in accordance with all these words.” (Exodus 24:8). That comes right after the people promise to do what the LORD has spoken (Exodus 24:7). It's a serious moment, so I'll just stand here quietly with my mustache.

They see the God of Israel, friends. Moses goes up with Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, and seventy of the elders, and they see Him (Exodus 24:9-10). Under His feet is something like a pavement of sapphire, as clear as the sky itself (Exodus 24:10). I think a hush fell over that whole group.

The answer is False, bakers. The text says, “But God did not lay His hand on the nobles of Israel; they saw Him, and they ate and drank.” (Exodus 24:11). God did not lay His hand on them. I think that's a big relief, and my mustache agrees.

They eat and drink, friends. The text says, “they saw Him, and they ate and drank.” (Exodus 24:11). Seeing God, and then eating and drinking. I think that's a gentle way for the moment to go, right after the verse says God did not lay His hand on them.

The word is instruction, bakers. The LORD says He will give Moses the tablets of stone, “…with the law and commandments I have written for their instruction.” (Exodus 24:12). Instruction is the word the LORD uses. I've been learning my own lessons from this book ever since I left that junk drawer.

The answer is Joshua his attendant, friends. Moses sets out with him and goes up on the mountain of God (Exodus 24:13). Joshua already fought the Amalekites for Israel (Exodus 17:10). He's the only one the text names for this part of the climb.

The answer is Aaron and Hur, bakers. Moses tells the elders, “Aaron and Hur are here with you. Whoever has a dispute can go to them.” (Exodus 24:14). Hur is the man who helped hold up Moses' hands during a battle, along with Aaron (Exodus 17:12). Two names, and a plain plan for any disputes while Moses is away.

The answer is True, friends. The cloud covers the mountain for six days, and “…on the seventh day the LORD called to Moses from within the cloud.” (Exodus 24:16). Six days, then the LORD calls. I'd have checked the oven six times, but this is a different kind of waiting.

The word is fire, bakers. The text says, “And the sight of the glory of the LORD was like a consuming fire on the mountaintop in the eyes of the Israelites.” (Exodus 24:17). That's the text's own comparison. It's what the Israelites saw on the mountaintop.

The answer is forty days and forty nights, friends. Moses “…remained on the mountain forty days and forty nights.” (Exodus 24:18). That's a long stretch. I waited years in that junk drawer, and I'm still not sure I'd have lasted on a mountain.
